title: Microsoft Purview Data Security Investigations: custom examination prompts for AI analysis
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap dates, custom examination workflow, billing, permissions and documented control paths are supported. Searches confirmed the narrowly stated documentation gaps. The checklist still recommends the cost estimator without a corresponding controls-table entry, a minor consistency issue.

claims.claim: A previously created custom examination prompt can be edited and re-run.

claims.claim: Microsoft's example custom prompts include extracting Protected Health Information.
claims.quote: "Identify any Protected Health Information (PHI) including patient names, medical record numbers, diagnosis codes, treatment information, and insurance identifiers."

claims.claim: Microsoft's example custom prompts include examining insider trading information.

claims.claim: Microsoft's example custom prompts include intellectual property exfiltration.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The licensing model is consumption, based on stored data and AI computing capacity.
claims.quote: Billing in Data Security Investigations is based solely on the combination of the amount of stored data and the associated computing capacity needed for AI analysis.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: DSI examination costs are not covered by a dedicated enterprise plan or licence.
claims.quote: It isn't based on a dedicated enterprise [plan or license]

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: DSI storage uses a pay-as-you-go storage meter.
claims.quote: The storage meter for Data Security Investigations uses the [pay-as-you-go billing](purview-billing-models) model.

claims.claim: Storage is charged per gigabyte per month for data associated with all investigations.
claims.quote: You pay for storage on a gigabyte (GB) per month basis for stored data associated with all investigations in your organization.

claims.where: summary; front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: AI examination consumes pay-as-you-go Data Security Investigations Compute Units, making cost variable.
claims.quote: Data Security Investigations uses the [pay-as-you-go billing](purview-billing-models) model for AI capacity. You need compute units for deep analysis and AI-related processing in your investigations. You pay only for the compute units you use.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Billing uses the Azure subscription and resource group linked during setup.
claims.quote:
**Azure subscription**: The Azure subscription you want to assign to the storage meter.
    2. **Resource group**: The resource group in your Azure subscription you want to assign to the storage meter.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Examination compute requirements are directly proportional to the size of the data examined.

claims.claim: DSI role-group permissions govern access to examination capabilities and their results.
claims.quote: To enable users to access Data Security Investigations capabilities and features in the Microsoft Purview portal, assign users the appropriate permissions.

claims.claim: Role-group membership is edited in Microsoft Purview at Settings > Roles and groups > Role groups > role group > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote:
Select **Settings** in the upper-right corner of the page, select **Roles and groups**, then select **Role groups** in the left navigation.
3. Select the *Data Security Investigations Admins* role group, then select **Edit**.
4. Select **Choose users**

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a member and grants the group's permissions.
claims.quote: When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group.

claims.claim: Role-group permissions can take up to 30 minutes to apply.
claims.quote: After you configure your role groups, it might take up to 30 minutes for the role group permissions to apply to assigned users across your organization.

claims.claim: AI capacity and processing location are configured in Microsoft Purview at Data Security Investigations > Setup tasks > Set up AI capacity > AI analysis data processing location.
claims.quote:

3. On the **Set up AI capacity**pane, complete the following fields:

claims.quote: To configure the AI capacity for Data Security Investigations, you must be a member of the *Data Security Investigations Admins* role group.

claims.claim: Billing configuration prerequisites list Global Administrator.
claims.quote:
To configure the storage meter and capacity for Data Security Investigations, you must have:
- The *Global Administrator* role.

claims.claim: Billing configuration prerequisites list resource group Owner or Contributor.
claims.quote: The resource group *Owner* or *Contributor* role.

claims.claim: Compute processing locations can be Australia/New Zealand, Europe, United Kingdom or United States.

claims.quote: You can opt in to having compute units provisioned and AI analysis processing done anywhere in the world to mitigate potential disruptions in case your primary location experiences high activity.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <date> -EndDate <date> -Operations DSIProbeJobSubmitted searches examination-start events.

claims.claim: Access to audit cmdlets requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs.
claims.quote: To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the *Audit Logs* or *View-Only Audit Logs* roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog is run in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Probing history records the creator's user principal name for each examination.
